j < n; ++j) {\n            #pragma omp single\n            {\n                // Diagonal element (implicit barrier publishes A[j][j] and success)\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    success = false;\n                } else {\n                    A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // All threads observe the same value, so they leave the loop together\n            if (!success) {\n                break;\n            }\n\n            // Off-diagonal elements of column j: independent across rows\n            #pragma omp for\n            for (size_t i = j + 1; i < n; ++i) {\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        #pragma omp for\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n                A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return success;\n}"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8847,"cache_read_input_tokens":17704,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8847},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3314cae8-5d79-42c4-a7bd-03820150cf12","uuid":"495ab203-2d1d-4fa1-9e51-b4615f89cb5e","timestamp":"2026-10-13T07:31:54.906Z","request_id":"req_011Cfyr3UeWWgubYrjFwdnH9"}

i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfyr8akzXfrgkdr4qfKfp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now always runs with OpenMP, and its output is byte-identical to the original at every matrix size I tested.\n\n**What changed** (only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`; no new files, executable name still `cholesky`):\n\n- **Decomposition (the timed kernel):** I switched from the row-oriented loop to a column-oriented one. For each column `j`, one thread computes the diagonal `A[j][j]`, then all rows `i > j` are updated in parallel. This sits in a single `omp parallel` region, so threads are forked once rather than per column. Each element keeps the original arithmetic and summation order, which is why results match exactly. The upper-triangle zeroing is also parallel.\n- **Failure path:** the non-positive-definite check still runs in column order, so it reports the same diagonal index as before, and a shared flag makes all threads exit together.\n- **Matrix generation (`B·Bᵀ`) and validation (`L·Lᵀ` and the error max-reduction):** parallelized. The `rand_r` fill stays serial so the random sequence is unchanged.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` linked. Configuration fails if OpenMP is missing rather than silently building serial code. `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` are kept.\n\n**Verification**\n- Clean build, no warnings. The binary links `libgomp`.\n- `-r` and `-v -r` output matches the original exactly, including the result hashes, for n = 1, 2, 3, 7, 64, 100, 255, 512, 1000. It also matches for `-n 0`.\n- The failure path (non-PD input) reports the same diagonal index as the original.\n- Timing at n=1024 (the decomposition itself, original 251 ms): 2 threads 127 ms, 4 threads 66 ms, 8 threads 40 ms, 16 threads 31 ms, 32 threads 17 ms, 64 threads 17 ms. Beyond 64 it gets worse: 128 threads 36 ms, 256 threads 208 ms. At n=2048 the original takes 2129 ms and the new code 174 ms on 256 threads.\n\n**Choices to be aware of**\n- I didn't add an `if` clause to skip OpenMP for small n, since you asked for the parallel approach to be unconditional. Small matrices therefore pay fork/barrier overhead.\n- I didn't add a thread-count line to stdout, to keep the output format that external tools may parse.
